reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, full local StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, and the supplied behavior context. Direct behavior findings for `TerminologyCapabilities` were absent; shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior was considered only as background per the review rules.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `TerminologyCapabilities` was FMM 0 / trial-use, so the compatibility burden is weaker than for mature or normative resources. That softens objections to tighter terminology capability modeling, but it does not erase breaks on central capability-discovery paths such as `codeSystem` and `codeSearch`.

overall.oneLineConclusion: TerminologyCapabilities keeps its identity but needs targeted migration for central terminology-capability metadata, especially `codeSystem.content` and `codeSearch`.

reasoning.thesisMd: `TerminologyCapabilities` is not removed or renamed, and much of the resource remains structurally recognizable. The material R4-to-R6 migration burden is concentrated in a few central terminology capability declarations: a mandatory `codeSystem.content` value, a replaced required `codeSearch` code set, new uniqueness/default-version constraints, and removal of the old `closure` subtree. That makes a targeted migration program realistic and often necessary, but it does not make every additional break irrelevant.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The shape is a moderate targeted remodel rather than a major model replacement. Existing instances without `codeSystem`, `codeSearch`, or `closure` may need little local work, but typical terminology server capability statements that enumerate code systems or code-search behavior need semantic decisions: how much content each code system exposes, how old code-search codes map to compose/expansion semantics, and whether duplicate declarations/defaults must be merged.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because migration is already needed for common, central paths, preventing every local validation break has less leverage than it would for a mostly unchanged resource. Still, low-cost preservation remains valuable where it can keep old valid instances valid without undermining R6 semantics. The strongest examples are transitional handling for `codeSearch` legacy codes and a softer introduction path for mandatory `codeSystem.content`.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The most standards-review-worthy alternatives are narrow. R6 could potentially retain `explicit` and `all` as deprecated `codeSearch` aliases while adding the new compose/expansion codes, and could have introduced `codeSystem.content` as optional, warning-level, or with an explicit unknown/unspecified value for one transition period. By contrast, keeping `closure` is only attractive if the underlying `$closure` operation still has an R6 home, and warning-only duplicate/default constraints would preserve ambiguous capability statements.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding in the supplied context targets `TerminologyCapabilities`. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior changes can affect generic clients, but they are not resource-specific drivers for this review.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's `Partial` migration-unavoidable result, `moderate-targeted-remodel` shape, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration` posture. The independent reason is not the finding count itself; it is that the hard breaks sit on central terminology capability metadata while several other findings are either cleanup chores or reverse-conversion concerns.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The main uncertainty is standards intent: the local inputs do not include official change notes, a `codeSearch` ConceptMap, or complete narrative for the fate of `$closure`. R6 is also a ballot package, so final content may change.

findingConsiderations.title: Each R6 codeSystem entry must now declare content mode
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the strongest resource-level driver. `codeSystem` is central to the resource, R4 had no native value to migrate, and choosing `complete`, `fragment`, `example`, `not-present`, or `supplement` can require terminology-server knowledge rather than a mechanical transform.

findingConsiderations.title: codeSearch required codes were replaced
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The same optional path remains, but the required enum was replaced. This can invalidate old instances and generated enum logic, and it is the clearest low-cost preservation candidate because deprecated legacy aliases or official mapping guidance could reduce migration cost without adding a duplicate field.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds error constraints requiring distinct code-system and version declarations
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real old-valid/new-invalid break, but it targets ambiguous duplicate code-system/version/default declarations. Once a resource migration is underway, grouping duplicates and selecting one default is a local data-quality cleanup rather than a reason to treat the whole resource as redesigned.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 removes the TerminologyCapabilities.closure subtree
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The removed subtree is a hard instance break for systems that advertised `$closure`, but expected prevalence appears narrow and preserving the element could mislead clients if `$closure` itself is gone from R6. It matters for migration policy, not as the dominant resource-level shape.

findingConsiderations.title: codeSystem.version.language now has a required all-languages binding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is only a potential break for non-language or private tokens. Because the element already means display language, a required language-tag binding is proportionate and does not materially change the resource-level migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds CodeSystem supplement capability declarations that R4 cannot natively represent
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new supplement declarations are optional and do not invalidate R4-to-R6 instances, but they can be semantically important for R6-to-R4 bridging. They warrant migration documentation or extensions for mixed-version ecosystems, not break-prevention pressure on the R6 base model.

findingConsiderations.title: Two local string fields changed to markdown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This may cause generated-model or renderer churn, but normal existing string values remain wire-compatible as markdown text. It is not a driver of resource-level migration.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the Resource $meta operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource-level behavior can affect generic clients, but it is not specific to `TerminologyCapabilities` and was not counted as a resource-level migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The shared search-parameter metadata change is relevant operational background for generic FHIR clients, but it does not change the local TerminologyCapabilities content-model judgment.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Ask the terminology work group to review whether R6 can preserve `codeSearch` legacy codes as deprecated aliases or publish an official ConceptMap/mapping note for `explicit` and `all`.
Review the transition strategy for mandatory `codeSystem.content`, especially whether an optional/warning/unknown transition would preserve R4 instances whose content mode cannot be inferred safely.
Document migration rules for `codeSystem` uniqueness/default constraints and for removed `closure`, including confirmation of the R6 status of the `$closure` operation.
Define an R6-to-R4 extension or loss-documentation strategy for supplement and global language-pack capability declarations when mixed-version clients need that information.

caveats: The review relies on local StructureDefinition, terminology, and report artifacts; official diff notes and JIRA rationale were not available in the supplied inputs.
No direct behavior findings targeted TerminologyCapabilities in the supplied context.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only.
The R6 source package is ballot content and may differ from the eventual published R6 release.
